newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore bars magazine over personal ads-publisher.
newsitem.headline: Singapore bars magazine over personal ads-publisher.

text.p: The Singapore government has not renewed the publication licence of IS Magazine over objections to its personal advertisement section, its publisher said on Tuesday.
"A licence the first time was not renewed but we have re-applied on the 16th of June," Gretchen Worth told Reuters.

The daily Straits Times newspaper reported that the Ministry of Information and the Arts (MITA) had found the magazine contravened guidelines against exploitation of sex to sell magazines and encouraged undesirable lifestyles.

"IS Magazine has flouted these guidelines by publishing items which are objectionable, for example, phonelines offering phone sex, ads which are lewd, and ads which promote unacceptable lifestyles such as homosexuality," the newspaper quoted a MITA spokesman as saying.
IS Magazine, a free fortnightly which covers lifestyle and entertainment, failed to get its publication permit renewed when it expired on June 12.
Worth said that along with the application for renewal of its licence, it had removed the personals pages immediately.
"Our feeling is that removing the personals page does actually take care of the objections that were raised to us, regarding why MITA did not renew the permit," Worth said.
She declined to comment on the nature of the advertisements.
A MITA official confirmed the licence had not been renewed but offered no other details immediately.
The Straits Times said MITA had warned the magazine more than once about carrying the offending items.
MITA was reported to be considering an appeal, but said the personal ad page was not a problem in itself.
The magazine is published by Hong Kong-based company Asia City Publishing Group and has an audited circulation of 25,000.
